EcoElectrica power station is NOT this terminal's captive power. It is the reason the terminal exists: a merchant cogeneration IPP (507/530 MW) that sells electricity to PREPA under a PPOA and receives LNG/gas from the terminal. Energy and gas flow terminal -> plant -> PREPA grid.

San Juan (PR) power station and San Juan II are NOT this terminal's captive power. The terminal was purpose-built to convert/fuel these PREPA units from liquid fuel to gas; both sell power to PREPA's grid. Gas flows terminal -> plant -> grid.

AES Colon (381 MW) and Gatun (670 MW) are NOT Costa Norte's captive power - they are merchant plants the terminal was built to fuel, each selling contracted capacity to Panama's distribution companies (ENSA, Edemet, Edechi) under PPAs. GEM's existing PowerPlantsSupplied entry is directionally correct.

Andres power station (319 MW) is NOT this terminal's captive power - it is a merchant combined-cycle plant selling under PPAs to distribution companies, fuelled BY the terminal. San Felipe (470 MW, construction, per the GOGPT prior) could NOT be independently re-verified in this pass (WebSearch budget exhausted; targeted lookups for San Felipe/ENADOM/TotalEnergies primary documents did not resolve) and was not found named in AES's FY2025 10-K, so its sponsor chain should be re-checked before assuming the same AES-integrated pattern applies.

The GOGPT 'Goldboro LNG power station' (180 MW, cancelled, captive=True) is the same 180 MW on-site generator plant documented in Pieridae's EA filings as a dedicated captive power source for the Goldboro LNG terminal ('to support the LNG facility and support services'). GOGPT's captive=True flag is CORRECT and matches the design intent and MW figure exactly. The 2.63 km coordinate offset from the LNG terminal's GEM point likely reflects that the power block, marine jetty, and main plant were assigned separate reference points within the same ~150 ha Goldboro Industrial Park parcel, not a genuinely distant/independent facility.

Solalban Energia (120 MW, Bahia Blanca) is NOT this terminal's captive power. It is a 2008-09 joint-venture power plant built specifically to supply Solvay Indupa's (now Unipar Indupa's) petrochemical/PVC production process at the Bahia Blanca Polo Petroquimico, with surplus commercialized to the wider grid via Energia Plus. TGS and its proposed LNG terminal are not the customer, owner, or beneficiary of Solalban's output in any source found -- the plants are unrelated industrial operations that happen to sit in the same industrial cluster.

Solalban Energia (120 MW, operating since Sept 2009, owned by Unipar Indupa/Albanesi) is NOT this terminal's captive power source: it predates Tango FLNG's arrival by a decade, has unrelated ownership, and serves the Bahía Blanca petrochemical complex rather than the YPF LNG dock. No source ties it to Tango FLNG/YPF's export operations.
